description.narrative: The project has benefitted from a climate and inclusion adjustment. The most significant expected project-level outcomes are improving the access, reliability, and affordability of electricity for consumers without access to power in Nigeria, with important environmental impact through GHG emissions savings. At the market level, IFC anticipates that the project will contribute to increase the competitiveness of the solar PV mini-grid market in Nigeria by using a programmatic approach to roll out mini-grid pipelines faster with demonstration potential in the region.

The proposed investment is to support PriVida Power Limited (the Company or PriVida) in deploying up to 75 mini-grid sites, totalling 26.5MW across Nigeria (Adamawa, Benue, Cross River, Delta, Edo, Gombe, Kano, Kogi, Kwara, Taraba). The mini-grid sites are expected to receive performance-based grants from the World Bank Nigeria Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up Project (DARES). The debt investment is part of an up to US$200 million IFC DARES Platform under which IFC is looking to provide similarly structured debt investments to several mini grid developers/operators.
